obj_2_recheck.objection_summary: iter1 major: deploy.sh:363 pushes to fork, but rollback.sh M15 forbids push. After local rollback, fork/main is AHEAD of HEAD; next deploy.sh's git fetch + merge could re-introduce bad commits. BA did not address fork-divergence consequence.

verification_checks.check: Advisory names divergence concretely (count + bad tag)
verification_checks.evidence: Line 103-104: script computes DIVERGENCE_AHEAD via `git rev-list --count HEAD..fork/main 2>/dev/null` and prints exact count. The literal advisory text in the worked example (line 404) reads: 'fork/main is now AHEAD of HEAD by 1 commit(s). The bad commit(s) you just rolled away from are still on the fork.' AC17 (line 272) enforces the literal string match. Concrete, not hand-wavy.

verification_checks.check: Path (a) uses --force-with-lease (correct safety mechanism, not bare --force)
verification_checks.evidence: Line 106: 'git push --force-with-lease=main:<fork/main commit at fetch time> fork main:main'. Line 414 in the worked example: 'git push --force-with-lease=main:0a1b2c3d fork main:main'. AC17 (line 274) enforces this exact form. BA chose --force-with-lease, not bare --force — operationally correct.

verification_checks.check: Path (b) tag-based forward roll makes operational sense
verification_checks.evidence: Line 107: 'plan a NEW dev-SHA that itself reverts or fixes the regression, and run a future deploy.sh <new-dev-sha> from /root/happy'. This is operationally correct: a forward-rolling fix avoids the force-push disruption when collaborators have already pulled. Worked example (line 418-425) elaborates correctly. Path (b) is sensible.

Line 108: '(a) for the common single-commit failed-deploy case, (b) for multi-collaborator scenarios where collaborators have pulled the bad commits'. Matches well-known practice — force-push is OK when nobody else pulled, otherwise prefer additive fix. AC17 (line 275) enforces the recommendation line.

verification_checks.check: AC17 static-grep enforcement of no git push/fetch in script body
verification_checks.evidence: AC17 (line 277): 'the script does NOT auto-execute git fetch or git push from anywhere in the divergence-advisory code path (verifiable via grep: git fetch and git push MUST NOT appear in the script body except inside comments)'. The intent — no executable git push/fetch calls — is clear. Drafting note: AC17 says 'except inside comments' but the printed copy-string for path (a) lives inside a here-doc/printf string literal (not a comment). A strict literal grep would flag the copy-string. This is a minor implementation-guidance issue: dev may need to use printf with escaped content, or the AC enforcement may match line-leading invocations only. Spec INTENT is correct and unambiguous; only the AC enforcement language has a small loophole. Not a blocking gap, but BA could optionally tighten AC17 to say 'except inside printable advisory strings and code comments' for full clarity. RESOLVED at the substantive level.

Line 109: 'The advisory must NOT auto-execute either path. The script prints, the operator decides.' Reinforced in AC17 (line 274): 'path (a) prints a copy-string for ... but the script DOES NOT execute it'. Operator-controlled, not script-controlled — correct.

objections.required_change: BA spec must EITHER (a) acknowledge in M8/M14-P3 that safe-daemon-restart.sh is currently absent and substitute concrete instructions (e.g., 'systemctl restart happy-daemon-jade.service' or whichever the actual SOP is); OR (b) declare safe-daemon-restart.sh authoring as a hard prerequisite that gates this cycle (rollback.sh cannot ship until safe-daemon-restart.sh exists); OR (c) add an AC requiring the dev subagent to verify the script's existence at runtime via [ -x ] and degrade gracefully when absent.

objections.issue: BA correctly identifies that rollback should be local-only (force-push footgun is real and codex's review point 11 caught it). HOWEVER, the spec does not address the asymmetric consequence: deploy.sh DOES push to fork (line 363 push --atomic for main + tags). After a local rollback, /root/happy/main is at OLDER commit while fork/main is at NEWER commit. The next operator who runs deploy.sh from /root/happy will: (a) git fetch fork — bringing the bad commit back as fork/main, (b) the cwd guard passes, (c) merge of dev-SHA might re-introduce the rolled-back code path silently if dev-SHA's history overlaps. This is a real operational bug: rollback that works once leaves the next deploy in a confused state.
objections.evidence: deploy.sh:362-371 explicitly pushes main + tags to fork. BA spec does not document the resulting fork-divergence after local rollback, nor instruct the operator on how to handle it.
objections.required_change: BA spec should add to the success epilogue (M15) a clear advisory: 'fork/main is now AHEAD of HEAD by N commits. Before the next deploy.sh, you must EITHER (a) accept the divergence and force-push main to fork (deliberate, consequential operation requiring sign-off) OR (b) document a tag-based forward path where the next deploy.sh starts from the rolled-back HEAD and explicitly excludes commits between PRE_ROLLBACK_HEAD and rollback target.' This is operational guidance, not a code change to deploy.sh.
